prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map divides the scene into three clear distance zones: near-field objects in bright white within arm's reach (~0.5–1.2 m), mid-range walls and furniture in medium grey (~1.5–2.2 m), and the distant dining room through the doorway in dark grey to black (~3–5 m). In the foreground, a person's head and chair back at the bottom-right (~0.5–0.8 m away, facing away from the camera wearer) sit roughly 0.5–0.8 m to the right of a white plastic highchair/seat and tabletop clutter at the bottom-left (~0.8–1.2 m away, also within arm's reach), with an X-back chair (~1.5–2 m) positioned just behind and between them against the left wall. Across frames 1 to 3, the camera wearer turns slightly leftward and downward—causing the bottom-right person's head to drop mostly out of the lower frame edge while the left-side white seat approaches the center—before turning back rightward in frames 4 and 5 to restore the initial view. The depth map reveals the 3D contours of the darkly lit foreground person, chair backs, and doorway walls that are hard to separate in the dim RGB frames, though it is unreliable inside the brightly backlit dining room (where the table and chairs wash out into flat black in frames 2–4) and along the blurred edges of the far-left clutter.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map labels parts of the scene across the 5 frames, identifying the foreground white seat (~0.8–1.2 m away on the left, within arm's reach), the mid-range X-back chair (~1.5–2 m away behind it), and the distant dining chair (~3.5–4 m away through the doorway) as chairs in frames 1 and 5, while detecting the heavily cropped person at the bottom-right (~0.5–0.8 m away, facing away toward the doorway) in frame 5. As the camera turns left from frame 1 to frame 3 and back right in frames 4 and 5, the detected masks change abruptly rather than tracking the continuous camera motion. In frame 5, the map usefully separates the dimly lit foreground person at the bottom-right and distinguishes the overlapping foreground and mid-range chairs on the left that blend into shadow in the RGB image. However, the segmentation is largely unreliable: it misclassifies the shadowed left clutter and chair region as a cat in frames 1 and 2 and as a person in frame 4, merges the right doorframe and foreground chair back into a single chair mask in frames 1 and 5, and misses nearly every object in frame 3 except the X-back chair.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank across all 5 frames, displaying only a small, isolated cluster of yellow keypoints at the bottom-left edge of frame 2 (~1 m away) and no magenta hand skeletons anywhere. From the RGB context, the only visible person is at the bottom-right within arm's reach (~0.5–0.8 m in front of and below the camera wearer), facing forward toward the doorway rather than looking at the camera wearer, with their body below the head occluded by the chair back and cut off by the bottom edge of the frame. As the camera turns left in frames 2 and 3, this person's head moves almost completely out of view at the bottom-right before reappearing in frames 4 and 5. Because of severe bottom-edge truncation and low lighting, the pose map adds no useful spatial information over the RGB strip and is unreliable, failing to detect the actual person on the right in every frame while hallucinating a stray cluster of body keypoints on the inanimate foreground objects in frame 2.
